provenance: explicit requirements; system-inferred diagnosis; local fallback implementation choices

diagnosis.finding: Six core native adapters boot the entire 978KB Pulse shell per preview; frames include unrelated UI, background, persistence and observers.
Every intersection exit destroys the renderer and clears its result; re-entry reconstructs it.
Square render viewport and forced canvas CSS cause letterboxing and inconsistent subject framing across portrait and landscape.
DOM and renderer state have no long-session resource budget.

diagnosis.source: live standalone feed observed in cloud browser
diagnosis.finding: Unavailable WebGL remains as text in blank cards and breaks visual comparison. Cloud browser cannot verify successful WebGL rendering.

locks.requirement: Repair lag while preserving procedural doom scrolling.
locks.choice: System policy: virtualize cards; maximum 3 live renderers, 1 native frame, 12 paused renderers, 48 offscreen posters; hide-page pause.

locks.requirement: Make visual selection consistent and show actual generator results.
locks.choice: Keep result posters when disposing; real preview with aspect preserved; failed All-feed generators skipped with failure evidence; descriptive unique labels.

locks.requirement: Run the issues through canonical Funnel, produce blueprint, route blueprint back, then implement.
locks.choice: MOOR.request original Page 0 -> queue; immutable blueprint + resolved spec and gates -> MOOR.request resolved Harness packet.

locks.requirement: Document automatic addition of new generators.
locks.choice: Same-origin wonder-generators.json descriptors or Haven.register; auto joins genome registry, selector, shuffled bag, capture/save and lifecycle. Require seeded preview bridge for reliable new adapters.

locks.requirement: Preserve grid scrolling, fullscreen scrolling, portrait/landscape toggle and organized saves.
locks.provenance: known user requirements and current implementation
locks.choice: Retain controls and file schema; replay recipes and settings; limits apply in both layouts.

implementationOrder: Register shared resource policy and virtualized history
Preserve posters and budget rendering by visible selection

Add automatic descriptor registry and integration guide

doneCriteria: Pulse and standalone load the same Haven and scroll policy release.
Long scroll keeps at most 60 mounted cards, 3 running renderers and 1 running native renderer; exiting feed tears down resources.
Returning to recently viewed cards shows retained real output without clearing the selection surface.
Portrait, landscape, resize and fullscreen preserve undistorted subject proportions and functional saves.
Six native core adapters load generated renderer bundles without Pulse chrome, spine, request bar or Wonder Feed recursion.
Unavailable generators do not leave text-only dead cards in the All feed; failure diagnostics remain queryable.
Adding a valid descriptor automatically registers a genome type and updates the mounted picker; duplicate/cross-origin definitions are rejected.
Original Page 0, requirements, system choices, routed envelopes and failed gates remain durable; no system choice is presented as owner confirmation.
limitations: Device-specific FPS and successful WebGL rendering require checks on the user's laptop/phone; resource caps are not an FPS guarantee.
Legacy same-origin preview adapters use DOM controls and best-effort canvas extraction. Deterministic pixel replay is not asserted for every old generator.
Captured posters are previews; saved full images/recipes remain in existing device storage. Previously evicted unsaved previews may be regenerated.
The canonical router queues intent and returns Harness packets; arbitrary code execution is performed here, not claimed as automatic router execution.
